newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR chief urges protection for Burundi refugees.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR chief urges protection for Burundi refugees.

text.p: The United Nations refugee chief urged Burundi's Tutsi-led military government on Wednesday to protect Hutu refugees returning from Tanzania after more than 120 were killed by troops last week.

U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata said: "I was deeply distressed by these killings. I repeat my call for all governments in the region to act in a humanitarian manner to the hundreds of thousands of people who have been displaced by conflicts there."
Ogata was also quoted as saying she had been assured by Burundian authorities that the culprits would be brought to justice.
France on Wednesday denounced the latest massacre and its foreign ministry called for steps to prevent future slaughters.

And Belgium said it feared Burundi was sliding towards greater ethnic violence. Its foreign ministry spokesman said the latest killings come on top of the reported massacre last month of around 3,000 civilians in the north of the country.
Some 750,000 Rwandan Hutus in Zaire were also forced home by Tutsi rebels after over two years in exile following 1994's Hutu-led genocide of minority Tutsis in Rwanda.
